core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aatirah is an Arabic-origin name meaning “Fragrant, perfumed, scented”.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Aatirah represents Arabic عاطرة (ʿāṭirah), the feminine form related to عاطر and the root ع ط ر, meaning fragrant or perfumed. Aatira and Aatirah are romanization variants associated with the same Arabic form.

etymology.morphology: Feminine active participle (fāʿilah pattern, feminine of عاطر) of عَطِرَ, built on the root ع ط ر.
etymology.etymological_meaning: From the root ع ط ر (ʿ-ṭ-r)
etymology.etymology_explanation: The form عاطرة is an established Arabic lexical item — the feminine of عاطر (ʿāṭir) — and Aatirah is the word itself used as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: No derivation beyond the documented Arabic form is asserted. Any etymology that attributes this spelling to a different root or language without a source should be treated as unverified.

faq.a: Aatirah represents Arabic عاطرة (ʿāṭirah), the feminine form associated with fragrant or perfumed.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aatirah?
faq.a: The recorded form عاطرة is Arabic; Aatirah is a romanization variant associated with Aatira/Aatirah.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is عاطرة (ʿāṭirah).

faq.q: What is the root of Aatirah?
faq.a: The form is associated with the Arabic root ع ط ر (ʿ-ṭ-r), related to fragrance.
Aatirah is used as a personal name in some Muslim communities, but the lexical meaning is not an exclusively religious definition.
This record does not establish Aatirah as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Aatirah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written عاطرہ and can be glossed as خوشبودار or معطر.
The supplied romanization is approximate; the underlying form عاطرة is commonly rendered ʿāṭirah.

faq.q: Is Aatirah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Aatirah as feminine, consistent with the Arabic form; regional frequency data is not supplied.
